bibitory: Of or pertaining to drinking or tippling.
billbug: A weevil or curculio of various species, as the corn weevil. See Curculio.
bitumenprocess: Any process in which advantage is taken of the fact that prepared bitumen is rendered insoluble by exposure to light, as in photolithography.
birdseed: Canary seed, hemp, millet or other small seeds used for feeding caged birds. BIRD'S-EYE Bird's"-eye`, a. 1. Seen from above, as if by a flying bird; embraced at a glance; hence, generalas, a bird's-eye view. 2. Marked with spots resembling bird's eyes; as, bird's-eye diaper; bird's-eye maple. BIRD'S-EYE Bird's"-eye`, n.
bitternut: The swamp hickory (Carya amara). Its thin-shelled nuts are bitter.
birthright: Any right, privilege, or possession to which a person is entitled by birth, such as an estate descendible by law to an heir, or civil liberty under a free constitution; esp. the rights or inheritance of the first born. Lest there be any . . . profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. Heb. xii. 16.
binaural: Of or pertaining to, or used by, both ears.
bicycling: The use of a bicycle; the act or practice of riding a bicycle.
bindheimite: An amorphous antimonate of lead, produced from the alteration of other ores, as from jamesonite.
bipinnatifid: Doubly pinnatifid. Note: A bipinnatifid leaf is a pinnatifid leaf having its segments or divisions also pinnatifid. The primary divisions are pinnæ and the secondary pinnules.
bistort: An herbaceous plant of the genus Polygonum, section Bistorta; snakeweed; adderwort. Its root is used in medicine as an astringent.
bipalmate: Palmately branched, with the branches again palmated.
bissextile: Leap year; every fourth year, in which a day is added to the month of February on account of the excess of the tropical year (365 d. 5 h. 48 m. 46 s.) above 365 days. But one day added every four years is equivalent to six hours each year, which is 11 m. 14 s. more than the excess of the real year.
bicapsular: Having two capsules; as, a bicapsular pericarp.
biseye: of Besee. (old) Chaucer. Evil biseye, ill looking. (old)
bisector: One who, or that which, bisects; esp. (Geom.) a straight line which bisects an angle.
binominal: Of or pertaining to two names; binomial.
billy: 1. A club; esp., a policeman's club. 2. (Wool Manuf.) A slubbing or roving machine.
biuret: A white, crystalline, nitrogenous substance, C2O2N3H5, formed by heating urea. It is intermediate between urea and cyanuric acid.
bilk: To frustrate or disappoint; to deceive or defraud, by nonfulfillment of engagement; to leave in the lurch; to give the slip to; as, to bilk a creditor. Thackeray. | 1. A thwarting an adversary in cribbage by spoiling his score; a balk. 2. A cheat; a trick; a hoax. Hudibras. 3. Nonsense; vain words. B. Jonson. 4. A person who tricks a creditor;
bicostate: Having two principal ribs running longitudinally, as a leaf.
bighorn: The Rocky Mountain sheep (Ovis or Caprovis montana).
bibber: One given to drinking alcoholic beverages too freely; a tippler; -- chiefly used in composition; as, winebibber.
birdeyed: Quick-sighted; catching a glance as one goes.
bilamellated: Formed of two plates, as the stigma of the Mimulus; also, having two elevated ridges, as in the lip of certain flowers.
biennial: 1. Happening, or taking place, once in two years; as, a biennial election. 2. (Bot.) Continuing for two years, and then perishing, as plants which form roots and leaves the first year, and produce… | 1. Something which takes place or appears once in two years; esp. a biennial examination. 2. (Bot.) A plant which exists or lasts for two years.
bickfordfuze: A fuse used in blasting, consisting of a long cylinder of explosive material inclosed in a varnished wrapping of rope or hose. It burns from 2 to 4 feet a minute.
biestings: The first milk given by a cow after calving. B. Jonson. The thick and curdy milk . . . commonly called biestings. Newton. (1574).
bicallous: Having two callosities or hard spots. Gray.
bidderyware: A kind of metallic ware made in India. The material is a composition of zinc, tin, and lead, in which ornaments of gold and silver are inlaid or damascened. [Spelt also bidry, bidree, bedery, beder.]
bifilar: Two-threaded; involving the use of two threads; as, bifilar suspension; a bifilar balance. Bifilar micrometer (often called a bifilar), an instrument form measuring minute distances or angles by means of two very minute threads (usually spider lines), one of which, at least, is movable; -- more commonly called a filar micrometer.
bilingualism: Quality of being bilingual. The bilingualism of King's English. Earle.
birdbolt: A short blunt arrow for killing birds without piercing them. Hence: Anything which smites without penetrating. Shak.
birthnight: The night in which a person is born; the anniversary of that night in succeeding years. The angelic song in Bethlehem field, On thy birthnight, that sung thee Savior born. Milton.
biodynamical: Of or pertaining to biodynamics, or the doctrine of vital forces or energy.
bilaminar: Formed of, or having, two laminæ, or thin plates.
bilboquet: The toy called cup and ball.
bilaminate: Formed of, or having, two laminæ, or thin plates.
biogenist: A believer in the theory of biogenesis.
bismuthine: Native bismuth sulphide; -- sometimes called bismuthite.
bivious: Having, or leading, two ways. Bivious theorems and Janus-faced doctrines. Sir T. Browne.
bimedial: Applied to a line which is the sum of two lines commensurable only in power (as the side and diagonal of a square).
birthwort: A genus of herbs and shrubs (Aristolochia), reputed to have medicinal properties.
bindingpost: A metallic post attached to electrical apparatus for convenience in making connections.
bittersweet: Sweet and then bitter or bitter and then sweet; esp. sweet with a bitter after taste; hence (Fig.), pleasant but painful. | 1. Anything which is bittersweet. 2. A kind of apple so called. Gower. 3. (Bot.) (a) A climbing shrub, with oval coral-red berries (Solanum dulcamara); woody nightshade.
bion: The physiological individual, characterized by definiteness and independence of function, in distinction from the morphological individual or morphon.
biding: Residence; habitation. Rowe. BIELA'S COMET Bie"la's com"et. (Astron.) A periodic coment, discovered by Biela in 1826, which revolves around the sun in 6.6 years. The November meteors (Andromedes or Bielids) move in its orbit, and may be fragments of the comet.
bituminous: Having the qualities of bitumen; compounded with bitumen; containing bitumen. Near that bituminous lake where Sodom flamed. Milton. Bituminous coal, a kind of coal which yields, when heated, a considerable amount of volatile bituminous matter. It burns with a yellow smoky flame.
bicipital: 1. (Anat.) (a) Having two heads or origins, as a muscle. (b) Pertaining to a biceps muscle; as, bicipital furrows, the depressions on either side of the biceps of the arm. 2. (Bot.) Dividing into two parts at one extremity; having two heads or two supports; as, a bicipital tree.
bicker: A small wooden vessel made of staves and hoops, like a tub. [Prov. Eng.] | 1. To skirmish; to exchange blows; to fight. (old) Two eagles had a conflict, and bickered together. Holland. 2. To contend in petulant altercation; to wrangle. Petty things about which men cark and…
binturong: A small Asiatic civet of the genus Arctilis.
bibliotaph: One who hides away books, as in a tomb. Crabb.
biliprasin: A dark green pigment found in small quantity in human gallstones.
biography: 1. The written history of a person's life. 2. Biographical writings in general.
billbook: A book in which a person keeps an account of his notes, bills, bills of exchange, etc., thus showing all that he issues and receives.
biliteral: Consisting of two letters; as, a biliteral root of a Sanskrit verb. Sir W. Jones. -- n. A word, syllable, or root, consisting of two letters.
biotite: Mica containing iron and magnesia, generally of a black or dark green color; -- a common constituent of crystalline rocks. See Mica.
bihydroguret: A compound of two atoms of hydrogen with some other substance. (old)
bibbs: Pieces of timber bolted to certain parts of a mast tp support the trestletrees.
biplicity: The state of being twice folded; reduplication. Bailey.
bichloride: A compound consisting of two atoms of chlorine with one or more atoms of another element; -- called also dichloride. Bichloride of mercury, mercuric chloride; -- sometimes called corrosive sublimate.
bi: 1. In most branches of science bi- in composition denotes two, twice, or doubly; as, bidentate, two-toothed; biternate, doubly ternate, etc. 2. (Chem.) In the composition of chemical names bi- denotes two atoms, parts, or equivalents of that constituent to the name of which it is prefixed, to one of the other component, or that such constituent is present in double the…
billman: One who uses, or is armed with, a bill or hooked ax. "A billman of the guard." Savile.
bing: A heap or pile; as, a bing of wood. "Potato bings." Burns. "A bing of corn." Surrey. [Obs. or Dial. Eng. & Scot.]
binder: 1. One who binds; as, a binder of sheaves; one whose trade is to bind; as, a binder of books. 2. Anything that binds, as a fillet, cord, rope, or band; a bandage; -- esp. the principal piece of timber intended to bind together any building.
bitterweed: A species of Ambrosia (A. artemisiæfolia); Roman worm wood. Gray.
biggen: To make or become big; to enlarge. [Obs. or Dial.] Steele.
bibliopegistic: Pertaining to the art of binding books. Dibdin.
bifoliolate: Having two leaflets, as some compound leaves.
bisulcate: 1. Having two grooves or furrows. 2. (Zoöl.) Cloven; said of a foot or hoof.
bidigitate: Having two fingers or fingerlike projections.
binocle: A dioptric telescope, fitted with two tubes joining, so as to enable a person to view an object with both eyes at once; a double- barreled field glass or an opera glass.
bilimbing: The berries of two East Indian species of Averrhoa, of the Oxalideæ or Sorrel family. They are very acid, and highly esteemed when preserved or pickled. The juice is used as a remedy for skin diseases. [Written also blimbi and blimbing.]
bicarburetted: Containing two atoms or equivalents of carbon in the molecule. [Obs. or R.]
bisulphate: A sulphate in which but half the hydrogen of the acid is replaced by a positive element or radical, thus making the proportion of the acid to the positive or basic portion twice what it is in the normal sulphates; an acid sulphate.
biologist: A student of biology; one versed in the science of biology.
birchen: Of or relating to birch. He passed where Newark's stately tower Looks out from Yarrow's birchen bower. Sir W. Scott.
bicallose: Having two callosities or hard spots. Gray.
bicuspidate: Having two points or prominences; ending in two points; -- said of teeth, leaves, fruit, etc.
bibacity: The practice or habit of drinking too much; tippling. Blount.
bitotree: A small scrubby tree (Balanites Ægyptiaca) growing in dry regions of tropical Africa and Asia. The hard yellowish white wood is made into plows in Abyssinia; the bark is used in Farther India to stupefy fish; the ripe fruit is edible, when green it is an anthelmintic; the fermented juice is used as a beverage; the seeds yield a medicinal oil called zachun.
binnacle: A case or box placed near the helmsman, containing the compass of a ship, and a light to show it at night. Totten.
binuclear: Having two nuclei; as, binucleate cells.
bishopdom: Jurisdiction of a bishop; episcopate. "Divine right of bishopdom." Milton.
billyboy: A flat-bottomed river barge or coasting vessel. [Eng.]
binervate: 1. (Bot.) Two-nerved; -- applied to leaves which have two longitudinal ribs or nerves. 2. (Zoöl.) Having only two nerves, as the wings of some insects.
bistoury: A surgical instrument consisting of a slender knife, either straight or curved, generally used by introducing it beneath the part to be divided, and cutting towards the surface.
billfish: A name applied to several distinct fishes: (a) The garfish (Tylosurus, or Belone, longirostris) and allied species. (b) The saury, a slender fish of the Atlantic coast (Scomberesox saurus). (c) The Tetrapturus albidus, a large oceanic species related to the swordfish; the spearfish. (d) The American fresh-water garpike (Lepidosteus osseus).
bivial: Of or relating to the bivium.
bilinguous: Having two tongues, or speaking two languages. (old)
bibulous: 1. Readily imbibing fluids or moisture; spongy; as, bibulous blotting paper. 2. Inclined to drink; addicted to tippling.
bird: 1. Orig., a chicken; the young of a fowl; a young eaglet; a nestling; and hence, a feathered flying animal (see 2). That ungentle gull, the cuckoo's bird. Shak. The brydds [birds] of the aier have… | 1. To catch or shoot birds. 2. Hence: To seek for game or plunder; to thieve. B. Jonson.
bide: 1. To dwell; to inhabit; to abide; to stay. All knees to thee shall bow of them that bide In heaven or earth, or under earth, in hell. Milton. 2. To remain; to continue or be permanent in a place or… | 1. To encounter; to remain firm under (a hardship); to endure; to suffer; to undergo. Poor naked wretches, wheresoe'er you are, That bide the pelting of this pitiless storm. Shak. 2. To wait for;
biflagellate: Having two long, narrow, whiplike appendages.
biscuit: 1. A kind of unraised bread, of many varieties, plain, sweet, or fancy, formed into flat cakes, and bakes hard; as, ship biscuit. According to military practice, the bread or biscuit of the Romans was twice prepared in the oven. Gibbon. 2. A small loaf or cake of bread, raised and shortened, or made light with soda or baking powder.
bigha: A measure of land in India, varying from a third of an acre to an acre.
biochemistry: The chemistry of living organisms; the chemistry of the processes incidental to, and characteristic of, life.
bitten: Terminating abruptly, as if bitten off; premorse.
bishoply: In the manner of a bishop. (old)
bignonia: A large genus of American, mostly tropical, climbing shrubs, having compound leaves and showy somewhat tubular flowers. B. capreolata is the cross vine of the Southern United States. The trumpet creeper was formerly considered to be of this genus.
bioscope: 1. A view of life; that which gives such a view. Bagman's Bioscope: Various Views of Men and Manners. [Book Title.] W. Bayley (1824). 2. An animated picture machine for screen projection; a cinematograph (which see).
biblicality: The quality of being biblical; a biblical subject.
billsticker: One whose occupation is to post handbills or posters in public places.
bibasic: Having to hydrogen atoms which can be replaced by positive or basic atoms or radicals to form salts; -- said of acids. See Dibasic.
birken: To whip with a birch or rod. (old) | Birchen; as, birken groves. Burns.
biweekly: Occurring or appearing once every two weeks; fortnightly. -- n. A publication issued every two weeks. -- Bi"week"ly, adv.
bitter: AA turn of the cable which is round the bitts. Bitter end, that part of a cable which is abaft the bitts, and so within board, when the ship rides at anchor. | 1. Having a peculiar, acrid, biting taste, like that of wormwood or an infusion of hops; as, a bitter medicine; bitter as aloes. 2. Causing pain or smart; piercing; painful; sharp; severe;
bishopric: 1. A diocese; the district over which the jurisdiction of a bishop extends. 2. The office of a spiritual overseer, as of an apostle, bishop, or presbyter. Acts i. 20. BISHOP'S CAP Bish"op's cap`. (Bot.) A plant of the genus Mitella; miterwort. Longfellow.
bisque: A point taken by the receiver of odds in the game of tennis; also, an extra innings allowed to a weaker player in croquet. | A white soup made of crayfish.
bicarinate: Having two keel-like projections, as the upper palea of grasses.
biotaxy: The classification of living organisms according to their structural character; taxonomy.
bicaudal: Having, or terminating in, two tails.
bimetallism: The legalized use of two metals (as gold and silver) in the currency of a country, at a fixed relative value; -- in opposition to monometallism. Note: The words bimétallisme and monométallisme are due to M. Cernuschi [1869]. Littré.
binny: A large species of barbel (Barbus bynni), found in the Nile, and much esteemed for food.
bitts: A frame of two strong timbers fixed perpendicularly in the fore part of a ship, on which to fasten the cables as the ship rides at anchor, or in warping. Other bitts are used for belaying (belaying bitts), for sustaining the windlass (carrick bitts, winch bitts, or windlass bitts), to hold the pawls of the windlass (pawl bitts) etc.
bisectrix: The line bisecting the angle between the optic axes of a biaxial crystal.
bicyclism: The art of riding a bicycle.
bipedal: 1. Having two feet; biped. 2. Pertaining to a biped.
billowy: Of or pertaining to billows; swelling or swollen into large waves; full of billows or surges; resembling billows. And whitening down the many-tinctured stream, Descends the billowy foam. Thomson.
biographer: One who writes an account or history of the life of a particular person; a writer of lives, as Plutarch.
bibliolatrist: A worshiper of books; especially, a worshiper of the Bible; a believer in its verbal inspiration. De Quincey.
biblical: Pertaining to, or derived from, the Bible; as, biblical learning; biblical authority.
biting: That bites; sharp; cutting; sarcastic; caustic. "A biting affliction." "A biting jest." Shak.
bibcock: A cock or faucet having a bent down nozzle. Knight.
bis: Twice; -- a word showing that something is, or is to be, repeated; as a passage of music, or an item in accounts. | A form of Bi-, sometimes used before s, c, or a vowel.
biceps: A muscle having two heads or origins; -- applied particularly to a flexor in the arm, and to another in the thigh.
billiards: A game played with ivory balls o a cloth-covered, rectangular table, bounded by elastic cushions. The player seeks to impel his ball with his cue so that it shall either strike (carom upon) two other balls, or drive another ball into one of the pockets with which the table sometimes is furnished.
bill: A beak, as of a bird, or sometimes of a turtle or other animal. Milton. | 1. To strike; to peck. (old) 2. To join bills, as doves; to caress in fondness. "As pigeons bill." Shak. To bill and coo, to interchange caresses; -- said of doves; also of demonstrative lovers.
bibliography: A history or description of books and manuscripts, with notices of the different editions, the times when they were printed, etc.
bister: A dark brown pigment extracted from the soot of wood.
bidet: 1. A small horse formerly allowed to each trooper or dragoon for carrying his baggage. B. Jonson. 2. A kind of bath tub for sitting baths; a sitz bath.
bilimbi: The berries of two East Indian species of Averrhoa, of the Oxalideæ or Sorrel family. They are very acid, and highly esteemed when preserved or pickled. The juice is used as a remedy for skin diseases. [Written also blimbi and blimbing.]
billion: According to the French and American method of numeration, a thousand millions, or 1,000,000,000; according to the English method, a million millions, or 1,000,000,000,000. See Numeration.
birthdom: The land of one's birth; one's inheritance. Shak.
bibelot: A small decorative object without practical utility. Her pictures, her furniture, and her bibelots. M. Crawford.
billard: An English fish, allied to the cod; the coalfish. [Written also billet and billit.]
bidarka: A portable boat made of skins stretched on a frame. [Alaska] The Century.
biorgan: A physiological organ; a living organ; an organ endowed with function; -- distinguished from idorgan.
birl: To revolve or cause to revolve; to spin. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott. | To pour (beer or wine); to ply with drink; to drink; to carouse. [Obs. or Dial.] Skelton.
birding: Birdcatching or fowling. Shak. Birding piece, a fowling piece. Shak.
bicipitous: Having two heads; bicipital. "Bicipitous serpents." Sir T. Browne.
birdcall: 1. A sound made in imitation of the note or cry of a bird for the purpose of decoying the bird or its mate. 2. An instrument of any kind, as a whistle, used in making the sound of a birdcall.
bigot: 1. A hypocrite; esp., a superstitious hypocrite. (old) 2. A person who regards his own faith and views in matters of religion as unquestionably right, and any belief or opinion opposed to or… | Bigoted. (old) In a country more bigot than ours. Dryden.
biometry: Measurement of life; calculation of the probable duration of human life.
birostrated: Having a double beak, or two processes resembling beaks. The capsule is bilocular and birostrated. Ed. Encyc.
billethead: A round piece of timber at the bow or stern of a whaleboat, around which the harpoon lone is run out when the whale darts off.
bibliopolic: Of or pertaining to the sale of books. "Bibliopolic difficulties." Carlyle.
bifold: Twofold; double; of two kinds, degrees, etc. Shak.
bidding: 1. Command; order; a proclamation or notifying. "Do thou thy master's bidding." Shak. 2. The act or process of making bids; an offer; a proposal of a price, as at an auction.
bise: A pale blue pigment, prepared from the native blue carbonate of copper, or from smalt; -- called also blue bice. Green bice is prepared from the blue, by adding yellow orpiment, or by grinding down… | A cold north wind which prevails on the northern coasts of the Mediterranean and in Switzerland, etc.; -- nearly the same as the mistral.
birthplace: The town, city, or country, where a person is born; place of origin or birth, in its more general sense. "The birthplace of valor." Burns.
billetdoux: A love letter or note. A lover chanting out a billet-doux. Spectator.
bight: 1. A corner, bend, or angle; a hollow; as, the bight of a horse's knee; the bight of an elbow. 2. (Geog.) A bend in a coast forming an open bay; as, the Bight of Benin. 3. (Naut.) The double part of a rope when folded, in distinction from the ends; that is, a round, bend, or coil not including the ends; a loop.
bilious: 1. Of or pertaining to the bile. 2. Disordered in respect to the bile; troubled with and excess of bile; as, a bilious patient; dependent on, or characterized by, an excess of bile; as, bilious symptoms. 3. Choleric; passionate; ill tempered. "A bilious old nabob." Macaulay. Bilious temperament. See Temperament.
bichir: A remarkable ganoid fish (Polypterus bichir) found in the Nile and other African rivers. See Brachioganoidei.
biology: The science of life; that branch of knowledge which treats of living matter as distinct from matter which is not living; the study of living tissue. It has to do with the origin, structure, development, function, and distribution of animals and plants.
biforine: An oval sac or cell, found in the leaves of certain plants of the order Araceæ. It has an opening at each end through which raphides, generated inside, are discharged.
bicarbonate: A carbonate in which but half the hydrogen of the acid is replaced by a positive element or radical, thus making the proportion of the acid to the positive or basic portion twice what it is in the normal carbonates; an acid carbonate; -- sometimes called supercarbonate.
biseptate: With two partitions or septa. Gray.
bitterspar: A common name of dolomite; -- so called because it contains magnesia, the soluble salts of which are bitter. See Dolomite.
bigotry: 1. The state of mind of a bigot; obstinate and unreasoning attachment of one's own belief and opinions, with narrow-minded intolerance of beliefs opposed to them. 2. The practice or tenets of a bigot.
biter: 1. One who, or that which, bites; that which bites often, or is inclined to bite, as a dog or fish. "Great barkers are no biters." Camden. 2. One who cheats; a sharper. [Colloq.] Spectator.
billholder: 1. A person who holds a bill or acceptance. 2. A device by means of which bills, etc., are held.
biparous: Bringing forth two at a birth.
bismer: 1. A rule steelyard. [Scot.] 2. (Zoöl.) The fifteen-spined (Gasterosteus spinachia).
bilifuscin: A brownish green pigment found in human gallstones and in old bile. It is a derivative of bilirubin.
bibliopolistic: Of or pertaining to bibliopolism. Dibdin.
bickering: 1. A skirmishing. "Frays and bickerings." Milton. 2. Altercation; wrangling.
biophotophone: An instrument combining a cinematograph and a phonograph so that the moving figures on the screen are accompanied by the appropriate sounds.
biostatics: The physical phenomena of organized bodies, in opposition to their organic or vital phenomena.
birdofparadise: The name of several very beautiful birds of the genus Paradisea and allied genera, inhabiting New Guinea and the adjacent islands. The males have brilliant colors, elegant plumes, and often remarkable tail feathers. Note: The Great emerald (Paradisea apoda) and the Lesser emerald (P. minor) furnish many of the plumes used as ornaments by ladies; the Red is P.
bicentenary: Of or pertaining to two hundred, esp. to two hundred years; as, a bicentenary celebration. -- n. The two hundredth anniversary, or its celebration.
birrus: A coarse kind of thick woolen cloth, worn by the poor in the Middle Ages; also, a woolen cap or hood worn over the shoulders or over the head.
bibliographer: One who writes, or is versed in, bibliography.
birdpepper: A species of capsicum (Capsicum baccatum), whose small, conical, coral-red fruit is among the most piquant of all red peppers. BIRD'S-BEAK Bird's"-beak`, n. (Arch.) A molding whose section is thought to resemble a beak.
bisk: Soup or broth made by boiling several sorts of flesh together. King.
billot: Bullion in the bar or mass.
bifid: Cleft to the middle or slightly beyond the middle; opening with a cleft; divided by a linear sinus, with straight margins.
billon: An alloy of gold and silver with a large proportion of copper or other base metal, used in coinage.
bibliomaniacal: Pertaining to a passion for books; relating to a bibliomaniac.
bibracteate: Furnished with, or having, two bracts.
bile: 1. (Physiol.) A yellow, or greenish, viscid fluid, usually alkaline in reaction, secreted by the liver. It passes into the intestines, where it aids in the digestive process. Its characteristic constituents are the bile salts, and coloring matters. 2. Bitterness of feeling; choler; anger; ill humor; as, to stir one's bile. Prescott.
bishop: 1. A spiritual overseer, superintendent, or director. Ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. 1 Pet. ii. 25. | To admit into the church by confirmation; to confirm; hence, to receive formally to favor.
bismuthyl: Hydrous carbonate of bismuth, an earthy mineral of a dull white or yellowish color. [Written also bismuthite.]
bitt: To put round the bitts; as, to bitt the cable, in order to fasten it or to slacken it gradually, which is called veering away. Totten.
billow: 1. A great wave or surge of the sea or other water, caused usually by violent wind. Whom the winds waft where'er the billows roll. Cowper. 2. A great wave or flood of anything. Milton. | To surge; to rise and roll in waves or surges; to undulate. "The billowing snow." Prior.
bipartient: Dividing into two parts. -- n. A number that divides another into two equal parts without a remainder.
billboard: 1. (Naut.) A piece of thick plank, armed with iron plates, and fixed on the bow or fore channels of a vessel, for the bill or fluke of the anchor to rest on. Totten. 2. A flat surface, as of a panel or of a fence, on which bills are posted; a bulletin board.
biographize: To write a history of the life of. Southey.
big: 1. Having largeness of size; of much bulk or magnitude; of great size; large. "He's too big to go in there." Shak. 2. Great with young; pregnant; swelling; ready to give birth or produce; | Barley, especially the hardy four-rowed kind. "Bear interchanges in local use, now with barley, now with bigg." New English Dict.
bigamous: Guilty of bigamy; involving bigamy; as, a bigamous marriage.
biaxial: Having two axes; as, biaxial polarization. Brewster. -- Bi*ax"i*al*ly, adv.
bigeye: A fish of the genus Priacanthus, remarkable for the large size of the eye.
bicameral: Consisting of, or including, two chambers, or legislative branches. Bentham.
bitters: A liquor, generally spirituous in which a bitter herb, leaf, or root is steeped.
birdie: A pretty or dear little bird; -- a pet name. Tennyson.
bickern: An anvil ending in a beak or point (orig. in two beaks); also, the beak or horn itself.
bisect: 1. To cut or divide into two parts. 2. (Geom.) To divide into two equal parts.
bibliology: 1. An account of books; book lore; bibliography. 2. The literature or doctrine of the Bible.
bibler: A great drinker; a tippler. [Written also bibbler and bibbeler.]

biopsychical: Pertaining to psychical phenomena in their relation to the living organism or to the general phenomena of life.
bike: A nest of wild bees, wasps, or ants; a swarm. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott.
birth: 1. The act or fact of coming into life, or of being born; -- generally applied to human beings; as, the birth of a son. 2. Lineage; extraction; descent; sometimes, high birth; noble extraction. Elected without reference to birth, but solely for qualifications. Prescott. 3. The condition to which a person is born; natural state or position; inherited disposition or tendency.
biprism: 1. A prism whose refracting angle is very nearly 180 degrees. 2. A combination of two short rectangular glass prisms cemented together at their diagonal faces so as to form a cube; -- called also optical cube. It is used in one form of photometer.
biserrate: 1. (Bot.) Doubly serrate, or having the serratures serrate, as in some leaves. 2. (Zoöl.) Serrate on both sides, as some antennæ.
birthless: Of mean extraction. Sir W. Scott.
bijoutry: Small articles of virtu, as jewelry, trinkets, etc.
bipupillate: Having an eyelike spot on the wing, with two dots within it of a different color, as in some butterflies.
bivalent: Equivalent in combining or displacing power to two atoms of hydrogen; dyad.
bibliographic: Pertaining to bibliography, or the history of books. -- Bib`li*o*graph"ic*al*ly, adv.
bitangent: Possessing the property of touching at two points. -- n. A line that touches a curve in two points.
bisselltruck: A truck for railroad rolling stock, consisting of two ordinary axle boxes sliding in guides attached to a triangular frame; -- called also pony truck.
binucleate: Having two nuclei; as, binucleate cells.
bimetallic: Of or relating to, or using, a double metallic standard (as gold and silver) for a system of coins or currency.
bito: A small scrubby tree (Balanites Ægyptiaca) growing in dry regions of tropical Africa and Asia. The hard yellowish white wood is made into plows in Abyssinia; the bark is used in Farther India to stupefy fish; the ripe fruit is edible, when green it is an anthelmintic; the fermented juice is used as a beverage; the seeds yield a medicinal oil called zachun.
biophore: One of the smaller vital units of a cell, the bearer of vitality and heredity. See Pangen, in Supplement.
bipartite: 1. Being in two parts; having two correspondent parts, as a legal contract or writing, one for each party; shared by two; as, a bipartite treaty. 2. Divided into two parts almost to the base, as a leaf; consisting of two parts or subdivisions. Gray.
biradiate: Having two rays; as, a biradiate fin.
bisaccate: Having two little bags, sacs, or pouches.
birthing: Anything added to raise the sides of a ship. Bailey.
billbeetle: A weevil or curculio of various species, as the corn weevil. See Curculio.
binoxalate: A salt having two equivalents of oxalic acid to one of the base; an acid oxalate.
bibliotaphist: One who hides away books, as in a tomb. Crabb.
bilocation: Double location; the state or power of being in two places at the same instant; -- a miraculous power attributed to some of the saints. Tylor.
biscotin: A confection made of flour, sugar, marmalade, and eggs; a sweet biscuit.
bittering: A bitter compound used in adulterating beer; bittern.
bipectinated: Having two margins toothed like a comb.
biplane: An aëroplane with two main supporting surfaces one above the other. | Having, or consisting of, two superposed planes, aërocurves, or the like; of or pertaining to a biplane; as, a biplane rudder.
birlaw: A law made by husbandmen respecting rural affairs; a rustic or local law or by-law. [Written also byrlaw, birlie, birley.]
bias: 1. A weight on the side of the ball used in the game of bowls, or a tendency imparted to the ball, which turns it from a straight line. Being ignorant that there is a concealed bias within the… | 1. Inclined to one side; swelled on one side. (old) Shak. 2. Cut slanting or diagonally, as cloth.
bident: An instrument or weapon with two prongs.
bicolligate: Having the anterior toes connected by a basal web.
bitterness: 1. The quality or state of being bitter, sharp, or acrid, in either a literal or figurative sense; implacableness; resentfulness; severity; keenness of reproach or sarcasm; deep distress, grief, or vexation of mind. The lip that curls with bitterness. Percival. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. Job vii. 11. 2. A state of extreme impiety or enmity to God.
biddy: A name used in calling a hen or chicken. Shak. | An Irish serving woman or girl. [Colloq.]
bigential: Including two tribes or races of men.
bibbe: To drink; to tipple. (old) This miller hath . . . bibbed ale. Chaucer.
birostrate: Having a double beak, or two processes resembling beaks. The capsule is bilocular and birostrated. Ed. Encyc.
birk: A birch tree. [Prov. Eng.] "The silver birk." Tennyson. | A small European minnow (Leuciscus phoxinus).
bimuscular: Having two adductor muscles, as a bivalve mollusk.
bittock: A small bit of anything, of indefinite size or quantity; a short distance. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott.
bibliolater: A worshiper of books; especially, a worshiper of the Bible; a believer in its verbal inspiration. De Quincey.
biogeny: (a) A doctrine that the genesis or production of living organisms can take place only through the agency of living germs or parents; -- opposed to abiogenesis. (b) Life development generally.
bicarbureted: Containing two atoms or equivalents of carbon in the molecule. [Obs. or R.]
biodynamic: Of or pertaining to biodynamics, or the doctrine of vital forces or energy.
bivouac: (a) The watch of a whole army by night, when in danger of surprise or attack. (b) An encampment for the night without tents or covering. | (a) To watch at night or be on guard, as a whole army. (b) To encamp for the night without tents or covering.
biograph: 1. An animated picture machine for screen projection; a cinematograph. 2. [Cf. Biography.] A biographical sketch. [Rare]
